segments.title: 第26章 那些年
segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 26: Those Bygone Years

That evening, the two old men, Ying Zhicheng and Li Guohong, drank themselves into a stupor at the dinner table. They collapsed onto the sofa to watch TV, still rambling and boasting to each other, before finally falling into a deep sleep.

Lin Xiuhong got up to clear the table, and Li Luo, along with Ying Chanxi, helped clean up, tidying both the living room and the kitchen.

"What do we do about these two?" Li Luo asked, turning to look at the two men on the sofa.

"Same as always," Lin Xiuhong said, rolling her eyes. "Just cover each of them with a blanket. Luckily, the sofa at the Xixis' is spacious."

After saying that, Lin Xiuhong went to get the blankets. But just then, Ying Zhicheng, who was supposedly asleep, suddenly shot his eyes open and sat up on the sofa. He groggily nudged Li Guohong.

"Get up, let's keep drinking."

Li Luo and Ying Chanxi looked at each other, then couldn't help but burst out laughing.

To their surprise, Ying Zhicheng still had some energy left. He staggered to his feet, walked over to the vertical cabinet next to the TV, and pulled out a guitar.

"Friends walk together for a lifetime!"

"Those days! Blech~"

"Hey, hey, hey!" Li Luo quickly ran over, tossed the guitar back onto the sofa, and supported Ying Zhicheng as they headed to the bathroom.

Once inside, Ying Zhicheng knelt before the toilet and immediately began to vomit profusely.

Ying Chanxi stood at the bathroom door, waving a hand in front of her nose in disgust. "So why do adults like drinking so much? It obviously tastes awful, and you get drunk if you have too much."

"Well..." Li Luo said with a smile as he gently patted Ying Zhicheng's back.

If he were fifteen, he definitely wouldn't have understood the reasons either.

But as a thirty-five-year-old, he knew all too well how hard the adult world was.

It wasn't the predictable, deterministic hardship of being a student, but a completely uncertain hardship, one with no standard answers, where accidents could happen at any time.

Of course, school was hard, but there was always a clear score to chase after.

But after entering society, scores alone were rarely enough to cut through all obstacles.

Alcohol didn't taste good, but when you wanted to cast all your emotions aside, it truly tasted wonderful.

If one sought a rare moment of blissful ignorance, there was nothing better to drink in the world.

"Maybe it's not the alcohol they're drinking," Li Luo said. "It's like how you like to listen to music to clear your head when you're in a bad mood. Drinking is the same."

"Then why not just listen to music? Drinking is bad for your health," Ying Chanxi was clearly a little upset about her dad drinking so much, worried about his health.

"My dad smokes, what can you do," Li Luo said helplessly. Seeing that Ying Zhicheng was about done, he said to Ying Chanxi, "Bring a towel over."

Ying Chanxi said "oh," and handed him a clean towel from the rack, then added, "You can't drink like this in the future, and no smoking either."

"You sure have a lot of rules," Li Luo said, helping Ying Zhicheng wipe his mouth. He looked much more comfortable after throwing up. Li Luo then helped him back to the sofa to lie down.

By now, Lin Xiuhong had come in with two blankets and covered the two men.

The snores of Ying Zhicheng and Li Guohong rose and fell, like a chaotic symphony rehearsal by a novice orchestra.

"Alright, pour two glasses of water and leave them on the coffee table. We'll deal with the rest tomorrow," Lin Xiuhong said with a look of resignation. "What about you two?"

"I'm going to study with Ying Chanxi for a while longer," Li Luo said brazenly.

"If you want to play on the computer, just say so. Stop putting on an act." Lin Xiuhong shot him a look and went back to their apartment across the hall to shower and get ready for bed. "Your dad might not be up tomorrow morning. Remember to go to the shop with me."

"Got it."

After seeing Lin Xiuhong off, Li Luo returned to the living room, but he didn't seem to have any intention of playing on the computer.

He picked up the guitar from the sofa and held it at a practiced slant in his arms.

Ying Chanxi, standing to the side, saw him holding the guitar so professionally and asked curiously, "You know how to play the guitar?"

"A little." Li Luo strummed a few notes on the guitar, getting a feel for it. Then, on a whim, he walked toward the door. "Come on, let's not wake them up."

"Where are we going?" Ying Chanxi followed Li Luo to the door, put on her shoes, and asked with blinking eyes.

"To the roof," Li Luo said, having already put on his shoes and started heading upstairs.

The buildings in Jincheng Community were only six stories high. They were relocation housing from the turn of the century, and the stairs led directly to the rooftop.

Carrying the guitar, Li Luo climbed all the way to the top. He breathed in the cool night air after the rain, stepped onto the slightly damp concrete floor, and sighed contentedly under the moonlight.

Ying Chanxi followed him up to the rooftop, still a bit skeptical. "You really know how to play?"

"Just request a song, then you'll know whether I can play or not." Li Luo found an open spot, turned to face Ying Chanxi, and got the feel of the guitar again, strumming a few random chords.

Seeing his confident expression, Ying Chanxi thought for a moment, then said, "Hmm... can you sing 'Those Bygone Years'?"

"That one?" Upon hearing the title, Li Luo searched his memory palace. When he recalled the lyrics, he was momentarily stunned.

"You can't?" Seeing his expression, Ying Chanxi thought he couldn't play it.

But in the next second, Li Luo chuckled softly and began to strum the strings.

"Back at the starting point again~"

"Your young, unseasoned face in my memory~"

"We've finally, arrived at this day~"

Li Luo's light voice floated across the rooftop, tinged with nostalgia and longing, instantly pulling Ying Chanxi into the song's atmosphere.

Ying Chanxi's small hands tapped gently to the melody. Her eyes reflected the boy's figure playing the guitar under the moonlight, and the corners of her mouth curved up slightly.

"...The heavy rain we missed in those bygone years~"

"...The love we missed in those bygone years~"

"How I want to embrace you~"

"Embrace the courage I missed~"

...

After the song ended, Ying Chanxi stood there, a bit dazed.

Li Luo glanced at her and couldn't help but laugh. "Hey, hey, you don't even know to applaud?"

Only then did Ying Chanxi snap back to her senses and clap vigorously. "That was so beautiful! And you really do know how to play the guitar?"

"I can only say I know a little," Li Luo said modestly.

He wasn't lying. After all, when he was making short videos, he had indeed learned a thing or two from a musician.

But he was by no means an expert.

It was more than enough to impress a young girl like Ying Chanxi, though.

"When did you secretly learn this?" After coming to her senses, Ying Chanxi couldn't help but ask suspiciously, "I had no idea."

"There's a lot you don't know." Fearing her endless questions, Li Luo immediately strummed the strings again and started singing the next song.

...

Over the weekend, Ying Zhicheng, for once, had no work. He stayed home to accompany Ying Chanxi and even cooked several meals himself to treat his daughter.

When it was time to leave on Sunday afternoon, in addition to her usual living expenses and school fees, he gave Ying Chanxi an extra 10,000 yuan.

"Dad?" Ying Chanxi was a little confused. "I don't usually spend this much."

"It's not just for you," Ying Zhicheng said. "Your Uncle Li's family won't take rent from you, but when you're staying over there, if you, Li Luo, or your classmates need to spend money on anything, don't be frugal, understand?"

Ying Chanxi blinked, clutched the money in her hand, and nodded forcefully.

Meanwhile, Li Guohong and Lin Xiuhong found time to go to the northern part of Yinjiang District to transfer the ownership of that apartment into their names.

But since the couple still had the shop to run, Lin Xiuhong called her younger brother, asking Li Luo's uncle to help with the move.

"My mom said to pack your things, like bedding, clothes, and all that. We'll take them over."

The following weekend, Li Luo took advantage of Ying Chanxi's day off to pop over to her place. "My uncle is coming with his car this afternoon to help us move our stuff to the new apartment."

"We're moving over already?" Ying Chanxi checked the date and couldn't help but ask, "Isn't there still more than a week until school starts?"

"What's wrong with that?" Li Luo asked, looking puzzled.

"So if we move, does that mean I'll be living there directly for the time before school starts?" Ying Chanxi asked again.

"Yeah," Li Luo said matter-of-factly. "You take the bus to school every day now, isn't it tiring?"

"Actually... it's alright, I guess?" Ying Chanxi said, then asked again in a small voice, "What about you?"

"Of course I'm moving in too," Li Luo said, looking at her strangely. "We're moving your computer over later, so I've got to go too, otherwise what would I play?"

Hearing this answer, Ying Chanxi didn't know whether to be happy or speechless.

"What? You thought I wasn't coming along?" Li Luo looked at her with amusement. "Tsk, tsk, do you want me to move in that badly?"

"I was just thinking you could cook for me," Ying Chanxi said stubbornly, turning her head away. "After we move, I won't get to eat Auntie Lin's cooking as often."

"My cooking isn't necessarily as good as my mom's."

"Heh." Hearing Li Luo say this, Ying Chanxi scoffed twice and narrowed her eyes at him. "Your cooking isn't good? Then why did the dishes on the day my dad came back taste so delicious?"

Li Luo blinked, feeling a little flustered under Ying Chanxi's gaze, and tried to bluff his way out. "That was because Uncle cooked well..."

"Who are you trying to fool?" Ying Chanxi said irritably. "My dad cooked himself for the next two days, and his food was nowhere near as good as the first day's."

"Oh, maybe my parents secretly went to help."

"Do you remember when I asked you to bring an umbrella to the bus station that day?" Ying Chanxi narrowed her eyes, her expression screaming 'there is only one truth'. "When we were heading back, we ran into Uncle and Auntie at the community entrance. How could they have had time to help my dad cook?"

"How do you remember things like that so clearly..." Li Luo couldn't help but mutter under his breath.

"So you really did help my dad cook?" Having confirmed it, Ying Chanxi flew into a rage, grabbing Li Luo's ear to settle the score. "At dinner that day, you even asked if Dad's cooking was good! How could you have the nerve to ask that!"

"Hiss... Stop, stop!" Li Luo grabbed Ying Chanxi's wrist tightly, bending over and begging for mercy. "Uncle's finger was injured, so I just helped him out a bit. Just pretend he made it."

"Hmph." Ying Chanxi hadn't really used any force at all. After letting go, she turned her back and stomped off to pack the clothes she was taking to the new place.

Li Luo, left in the living room, was also at a loss for words. He thought to himself, how could Uncle Ying be so tactless? Doesn't he have a clear understanding of their respective cooking skills?

Who sells out their own teammate like that?

"Go to the study and sort out the computer. I don't know what needs to be taken." Halfway through her packing, Ying Chanxi poked her head out of the bedroom. After speaking, she added a warning, "If you dare trick me again, I'll have Auntie Lin bring the computer back so you can't play with it anymore."
